Figure 4 presents a comparison of the primary semantic domains of verbs across different languages, with two sub-figures labeled (a) and (b). 

The horizontal axis represents different languages, and the vertical axis on the left side displays frequency values ranging from 0 to 4,000, marked at intervals of 1,000. 

In sub-figure (a), there are grouped bars representing the distribution of primary semantic domains for verbs that support or spur actions. The colors used for each domain are blue, orange, red, green, and dark blue. The blue bars are the longest, reaching approximately 900 in one of the languages, while the shortest bars are around 50.

In sub-figure (b), there are also grouped bars showing the distribution of primary semantic domains for verbs that undertake or bear actions. Similar colors are used, but the distribution appears different. The blue bars again dominate, reaching up to around 900 in one language.

The bars in both sub-figures are not sorted in any specific order, and no particular bar is visually emphasized beyond the color coding and grouping. 

Overall, Figure 4 provides a visual representation of how verbs across different languages are distributed in terms of their primary semantic domains related to actions that either support/spur or undertake/bear.
